h1: The 6 Best Large Button Calculators Under $20 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 large button calculators scored on display size, key feel and power source, from 5 inch LCD models to memory-key desk units.
summary: The pendancy 5-inch LCD desktop calculator is the best large-display pick, with a 12-digit readout tilted at 30 degrees and color-coded keys. The yxzzhx matches the 5 inch screen with solar or battery power. For raised, easy-to-find keys, choose the M&G 12-digit model, and the HIHUHEN is the one to buy if you need memory and percent keys.
intro: Most large-button calculators are sold on the size of the keys, but the display does more of the real work. A tiny readout on a big-key body forces you to squint and lean in, which defeats the point. The better question is how large the digits are, how the screen is angled, and whether the keys give your fingertip a clear target.

That is how we ordered these six. Each desk calculator was scored on the Primea framework for display size and tilt, key size and feedback, power flexibility between solar and battery, and any extra functions like memory keys. All of them sit in the under $25 price bucket, so the decision comes down to layout, not budget.

products.name: pendancy 5-Inch LCD Desktop Calculator
products.verdict: A 5 inch, 12-digit LCD tilted at 30 degrees with giant, color-coded keys.
products.description:
The pendancy leads on the part that matters most: a 5 inch LCD with a 12-digit readout and a 30 degree display tilt, so you read the digits without hunching over the desk. The giant response keys come in color-coded groups, orange, blue and gray on a silver ABS body, which lets you find the operator keys by color before you read the labels.

It ranks above the yxzzhx by a small margin because the key coding is a real usability aid, while both share the 5 inch screen. Compared with the 12-digit mid-size models, you get a bigger display at the cost of a larger desk footprint.

A strong pick for anyone who squints at standard calculators. Caveat: the listing does not describe the power source clearly, so confirm whether it uses solar, battery or both before relying on it.
pros: 5 inch display is easy to read
products.idealFor: Anyone who struggles to read small calculator screens.

products.name: yxzzhx 5-Inch Two-Way Power Desktop Calculator
products.verdict: Another 5 inch, 12-digit display, powered by solar or two included AA batteries.
products.description:
The yxzzhx pairs a 5 inch LCD showing 12 digits with a tilted screen angle for comfortable desk viewing. It runs on solar or battery, and two AA batteries are included, so it works under a window or in a dim office without ordering anything extra. Two-way power avoids the dead-calculator problem that plagues solar-only units.

It sits just behind the pendancy because it lacks color-coded key groups, a feature that speeds up finding the right button. Against the M&G, you get a much larger screen, but the keys are less distinctly raised.

A good fit for office desks and family kitchens. Caveat: AA batteries last a long time in a calculator, but you still need to replace them eventually, and the listing does not state a lifespan.
products.idealFor: Offices and kitchens with variable lighting.

products.name: M&G 12 Digit Desk Calculator with Embedded Big Buttons
products.verdict: A 12-digit large LCD with raised, sturdy keytops you can find by feel.
products.description:
M&G builds its calculator around embedded big buttons with a raised key design, so each keytop stands proud of the body and your finger can find it by touch. The keys are sturdy plastic, and the 12-digit LCD is large. Power comes from solar plus an included AAA battery.

It ranks third because the screen is smaller than the 5 inch pendancy and yxzzhx, but the raised keys are a genuine advantage for fast, accurate typing. Against the CATIGA, the keys are squarer and clearly separated.

Best for people who care more about key feel than screen size. Caveat: raised keys catch crumbs and dust, so wipe it down regularly if it lives in a kitchen.
products.idealFor: Fast typists who want clear keys.
products.skipIf: You need the largest possible display.

products.name: CATIGA 12 Digit Desktop Calculator with Round Keys
products.verdict: Big round responsive keys and an angled 12-digit display for study and home use.
products.description:
CATIGA gives you big round keys with a responsive feel and an angled 12-digit LCD. The simple four function layout, add, subtract, multiply and divide, suits students and home budgeting. It runs on solar plus battery, so it keeps working in low light.

It ranks fourth because round keys are easier to hit with a fingertip than small squares, but they are not raised or color coded like the top picks. Against the DXNIKAM, the round shape is the standout, while the DXNIKAM adds anti-slip feet.

A fit for study desks and household bills. Caveat: with only four functions there is no memory or percent key, so tax and tip calculations need extra steps.
products.skipIf: You need percent or memory functions.

products.name: HIHUHEN 12 Digit Solar and Battery Calculator
products.verdict: A 12-digit LCD with memory keys, percent, square root and a rounding setting.
products.description:
HIHUHEN is the feature-rich option: a 12-digit Japanese LCD with memory keys MC, MR, M+ and M-, plus percent, square root and plus/minus keys and a rounding setting. It runs on solar with one AA battery as backup. If you handle invoices, tax or recipe scaling, the memory keys alone save a lot of re-entering.

It ranks fifth because its focus is functions, not size. The keys are not marketed as extra large, so it asks more of your eyes and fingers than the 5 inch models. Against the CATIGA, it adds memory and percent but loses the round-key advantage.

Ideal for small business bookkeeping on a budget. Caveat: more keys mean smaller keys, so low-vision users should lean on the pendancy or yxzzhx instead.
cons: Keys not marketed as extra large
products.idealFor: Small business owners handling invoices and tax.
products.skipIf: Key size and screen size are your top priorities.

products.name: DXNIKAM 12 Digit 4 Function Desk Calculator
products.verdict: A no-frills four function calculator with big buttons and anti-slip foot pads.
products.description:
DXNIKAM keeps things plain: a 12-digit large display, four function layout and big responsive buttons, with two anti-slip foot pads that stop it creeping across the desk when you press hard. Power is solar plus battery. The simple layout is easy to learn, which matters when the calculator is shared.

It ranks last only because it has the fewest standout features. There are no color-coded keys, raised key shapes or memory functions to separate it from the CATIGA or M&G. What it does have is a stable base.

Good for a family drawer calculator or a shared counter. Caveat: the listing gives no display tilt or exact size, so check the product images before expecting the readability of the 5 inch models.
products.skipIf: You want the biggest screen or advanced functions.

methodology.title: Display size and angle
methodology.description: Screen diameter, digit count and tilt were scored first because readability is the main reason to buy a large-button model.

methodology.title: Key size and feel
methodology.description: Giant, raised or round keys were compared for how clearly they give a fingertip a target.

methodology.title: Power flexibility
methodology.description: Solar plus battery combinations were favored over single-source models, since each fails in different light conditions.

methodology.title: Functions
methodology.description: Memory, percent and square root keys added points, balanced against the key crowding they cause.

methodology.title: Stability and value
methodology.description: Anti-slip feet, body build and the under $25 price bucket were weighed together.

whatMatters.detail: A bigger screen shows larger digits that are easier to read at arm's length. A 5 inch LCD is substantially larger than a standard 3 inch one. Check the stated display diameter and the digit count, and remember that 12 digits is enough for most household and business sums.

Tilted screens reduce glare and neck strain on a flat desk. Look for a stated angle, like the pendancy's 30 degrees, or an angled display. A flat screen under overhead lights can reflect light directly into your eyes.

Giant, round or raised keys give fingertips clearer targets and reduce mispresses. Closely packed small keys cause errors. Check the listing for words such as giant, big or raised, and think about whether you type by feel or by sight.

Solar powers a calculator in bright light, while a battery covers dim rooms. Dual power avoids a dead unit. Look for solar plus battery, and confirm whether a battery is included, as with the yxzzhx's two AA cells.

Four function calculators are simple, while memory and percent keys help with tax, invoices and recipes. Extra keys crowd the layout. Decide whether you need MC, MR, M+ and M-, and accept smaller keys if you do.

faq.q: Are large-button calculators accurate for bookkeeping?
faq.a: Yes, all six use 12-digit displays. For bookkeeping, the HIHUHEN adds memory keys and a rounding setting, while the pendancy and M&G are better for plain addition where readability and key feel matter more.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with big-key calculators?
faq.a: Assuming big keys mean a big screen. The DXNIKAM and CATIGA have large buttons but standard 12-digit displays, while the pendancy and yxzzhx have a 5 inch LCD. Check display size separately.

faq.q: Is the pendancy worth it over the yxzzhx?
faq.a: If you want color-coded keys, yes. Both have a 5 inch, 12-digit LCD, but the pendancy groups keys by color, while the yxzzhx includes two AA batteries and clearly lists solar or battery power.

faq.q: How do I set up a solar calculator?
faq.a: Place it in bright light and it powers on automatically. For models with batteries, such as the yxzzhx with two AA cells or the M&G with an AAA, insert the battery for backup in dim rooms.

faq.q: How do I maintain a calculator with raised keys?
faq.a: Wipe the keys with a lightly dampened cloth and avoid spraying liquid on the body. The M&G's raised keys collect dust, so tilt it and brush crumbs out from time to time.

faq.q: Can these be used in low light?
faq.a: Models with batteries can. The yxzzhx, M&G, HIHUHEN, CATIGA and DXNIKAM list solar plus battery power, so they keep working under dim lamps when solar alone would fail.

finalTake: The pendancy 5-Inch LCD Desktop Calculator is the best choice for anyone who values readability, with a 12-digit display, 30 degree tilt and color-coded giant keys. The yxzzhx is a close second thanks to included batteries, and the M&G suits those who type by feel. Pick the display and key style first, then add functions only if you need them.
